newsitem.title: USA: Western U.S. states urge TV to delay naming winners.
newsitem.headline: Western U.S. states urge TV to delay naming winners.

text.p: Top officials from eight Western states urged U.S. television networks Wednesday not to project winners of next Tuesday's elections until after the polls have closed in the West.

The networks often project the winner of the presidential race soon after the polls close in the East but while polls in the West, where there is a time difference of up to three hours, are still open.
Officials in the West have complained that voters there may not have an incentive to vote, which could affect other races and issues on the ballot.

A letter to network news executives, signed by the secretaries of state of California, Washington, Idaho, Nevada, Montana, Oregon and Arizona and by the lieutenant-governor of Utah, asked the networks to "refrain from projecting any winners until the polls close across America."

"On behalf of the millions of voters who call the great American West home, we urge you not to abridge their right to participate in the process of electing the president and Congress of the United States by broadcasting early projections on election day," the officials wrote in the letter released by California Secretary of State Bill Jones.

The officials said an early projection by the news media of the winner of the contest between President Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole "will almost certainly have a chilling effect on voter turnout."

An early projection of which party appears set to win control of Congress "could have an even more devastating impact on a number of 'too close to call' congressional races, not to mention state and local contests," they wrote.

"Candidates and voters deserve to play on the same level playing field as their East coast counterparts ... We must not allow our election day to become the equivalent of a drive-through democracy, where expediency is gained at the expense of fairness," they added.

The officials singled out the 1980 elections, when NBC projected Ronald Reagan the winner nearly three hours before the polls closed on the West coast. ABC and CBS made projections soon afterward and then-President Jimmy Carter made his concession speech when there was still more than an hour left to vote in Western states, they said.
Turnout dropped by about two percent in California after the 1980 announcement, and election officials reported that many voters left the polls without casting their ballots, the officials said.
Jones predicted that 71 percent of the 15.6 million voters on California's rolls will to go the polls next Tuesday.
